title: Adaptive chunk reclamation and CUDA scaling — field notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an exploratory debugging thread on persistent GPU memory pressure and intermittent OOM spikes in multi-tenant inference pools. Focus: allocator behavior (cudaMalloc/cudaFree + async pools), workspace chunk sizing, and an experiment for adaptive chunk reclamation that reduces fragmentation without impacting tail latency.

Context / Why this surfaced:
- Multiple customer incidents (high token workloads) had non-deterministic OOMs despite nominally sufficient reserved capacity.
- Observed: steady-state memory usage stable, but occasional ~300–700MB jumps triggering cudamalloc retries and eviction cascades.
- Hypothesis: allocator free-list fragmentation combined with long-lived pinned blocks (prefetching/kv-cache pinned tensors) prevented coalescing, and async allocation paths amplified retry loops.

Instrumentation used (quick list):
- nvml (nvidia-smi sampling at 1s), GPU driver meminfo, and per-alloc tracing via custom malloc interceptor (LOG_ALLOC with stack id).
- Heap histogram export (epoch snapshots) + free-list snapshot from our mempool at 100ms intervals during replay.
- Flight recorder traces capturing sequence lengths, batch sizes, model variants, and which code path requested workspace.
- Synthetic replay harness: dense 2–8 token length fanout simulating chat bursts.

Observed allocation patterns:
- Two dominant allocation classes in traces: large contiguous workspace requests (20–200MB) for attention KV, and many small ephemeral allocations (2–16KB) from tensor reshapes and scratchpads.
- Large requests often came shortly after small allocations in the same stream; free-list showed many small free blocks interleaved with a few large reserved slabs.
- cudaMallocAsync fallback triggered when pool slack < requested size. Fallback led to immediate cudaMalloc followed by slow allocation and sometimes host pinned fallback.

Representative log snippet (trimmed):
[2025-09-15 13:07:01.841] pool: request 76.3MB stream=0 ctx=worker-7
[2025-09-15 13:07:01.842] pool: small free run: 32 x 8KB blocks scattered
[2025-09-15 13:07:01.842] pool: no contiguous 76.3MB found -> calling cudaMallocAsync fallback
[2025-09-15 13:07:01.982] cudaMallocAsync: success (allocated on device) 76.3MB, but fragmentation metric increased
[2025-09-15 13:07:01.995] tail: eviction triggered for slab-4 (128MB) -> moved to host-pinned staging -> reinstated

Key evidence pointing to fragmentation/coalescing issue:
- Heap histograms before/after OOM show many small free blocks totaling > requested size, but not contiguous.
- Coalescing metrics (our mempool) rarely trigger for free events that are separated by intervening allocations on other streams — our arena boundary rules partitioned memory by stream affinity to reduce lock contention, but this reduced opportunities to merge.
- When we force a synchronous consolidation pass (experimental code), observed >40% reduction in cudaMallocAsync fallbacks on replay. However, consolidation costs spiked short-term latency.

Root-cause hypothesis (condensed):
1) Multi-stream allocation interleaving + per-stream/fine-grained arenas reduces lock contention but fragments address space across arenas.
2) Long-lived pinned objects (kv-cache reservations, prefetch buffers) hold slabs that fragment the global free map; small frees cannot be coalesced across arena boundaries.
3) cudaMallocAsync fallback path (host-side cudaMalloc or device-side new mapping) is invoked when contiguous block not found; fallback both magnifies transient pressure and precludes pool optimizations (it bypasses delayed freeing semantics).

Experiments run and results:
Experiment A: forced arena coalescing every N frees (N=128) for 10s windows- Result: fallback rate dropped 42% on replay; 95th tail latency increased ~8% during coalescing window; average latency unaffected.

Experiment B: adaptive chunk reclamation (prototype)- Idea: identify candidate arenas with low recent allocation rate but many fragmented free spans; during idle periods reclaim and defragment by migrating long-lived allocations to a compact slab and release freed addresses to a global arena.- Result: fallback rate down 35% over 1 hour test; tail latency impact negligible when reclaiming scheduled with background worker; memory compaction cost amortized across idle cycles.

Experiment C: adjust workspace sizing policy to prefer power-of-two rounding up to next 16MB for large allocations- Result: slightly higher peak memory (5–7%) but a reduced fragmentation footprint and 18% fewer fallbacks for sizes >32MB. Tradeoff: increased nominal memory reservation.

Micro-observations (useful notes):
- Small allocation churn (2–16KB) created many freelist tombstones; our allocator's tombstone reclamation path ran only on cross-arena merges.
- Streams that do prefetching (L0) had sticky allocations that were not freed for long durations, creating holes between active arenas.
- CUDA driver version differences: 12.2 shows marginally better cudaMallocAsync coalescing behavior than 12.1 in our baseline tests — driver upgrade reduced fallback frequency by ~6% (worth noting for customer infra).

Short-term mitigations for production (recommended, and low risk):
- Opt-in adaptive chunk reclamation background worker (toggle via runtime flag) — moderate risk, high benefit.
- Increase prefetch buffer sizing policy so we use fewer, larger prefetch blocks (reduces number of pinned slabs). Configurable per-model.
- Conservative workspace rounding policy for heavy models: round to nearest 8–16MB to improve chance of contiguous allocation.
- Alerting: track cudaMallocAsync fallback spike as an SLI for fragmentation; create a Grafana panel with fallback-rate, free-span-count, and pool-contiguous-failures.

Longer-term design proposals (engineering tradeoffs):
- Global defragmenter that compacts live allocations by migrating data during low-util windows. Complexity: safe live-migration of GPU tensors (must preserve pointers across kernels) and interaction with stream synchronization.
- Hybrid arena policy: keep per-stream arenas for small churn, but maintain a shared large-arena for big contiguous allocations (>32MB) with stricter placement heuristics. This reduces fragmentation for the important class while preserving low-lock contention for small allocs.
- Kernel-aware placement: use model/sequence-length hints to pre-reserve contiguous slabs in the shared arena for upcoming large requests (predictive reservation). Needs robust failure handling.

Operational replay / repro steps (so SRE/dev can reproduce):
1) Checkout branch bench/frag-repro on playground (linked PR).
2) Run replay harness: ./replay --profile workload/chatburst --fanout 8 --seq-dist "2:0.2,16:0.5,64:0.3" --duration 600s
3) Enable allocator tracing: export REDWOOD_ALLOC_TRACE=1 and set trace-output=/tmp/alloc-trace.log
4) Monitor fallback counter in metrics (metrics.alloc.cudamallocasync_fallback) and sample heap hist every 10s.
5) Optional: force coalesce with admin endpoint POST /admin/arena/coalesce?force=true

Open questions (to address in followups):
- Exact ROI of driver upgrades across our supported fleet. We need test matrix: driver x cuda runtime x instance type.
- Safe semantics for live-migrate: do we accept brief kernel stalls? How to ensure correctness for asynchronous inference pipelines?
- Telemetry: what lightweight signals can predict an imminent fallback (and therefore trigger pre-emptive compaction)?

Immediate action items (owner tags):
- [Aisha] Roll out background reclaim worker as opt-in flag behind runtime feature gate (ETA 1 week, low-risk smoke tests).
- [Marco] Add Grafana panels and alert rule for follback-rate and contiguous-failure-rate (ETA 3 days).
- [Lina] Run driver upgrade matrix on k80/p4d/p4d-v3 fleet subset and capture fallback-delta (ETA 2 weeks).
- [Rahul] Prototype hybrid-arena placement heuristic (ETA spike prototype 3 weeks).

Appendix: quick checklist for incident runbooks
- If OOMs spike: enable background reclaim, increase workspace rounding to 16MB, and drain prefetchers for the affected pool.
- Capture one alloc trace and one heap hist before/after mitigations. Attach to JIRA.

Rough priority summary:
- Low-effort, high-value: background reclaim worker behind flag, Grafana alerting, workspace-rounding knob.
- Medium-effort: hybrid arena for large allocations, pre-reservation hints.
- High-effort: safe global compactor (requires design review + sync contract with kernels).

Notes to self / free-form thoughts:
- There may be interplay with NUMA on multi-GPU instances if we ever attempt cross-device migration. For now, keep compaction intradev.
- Consider exposing a model annotation to prefer dense contiguous allocations for top-K layers that touch KV-cache.

-- end --
